einzeiler: Investigative reporting helps overturn a wrongful conviction after two decades.
kurzfassung: Marty Tankleff fought for decades to overturn his wrongful murder conviction after being coerced into a confession as a teenager. Private investigator Jay Salpeter uncovered new witnesses, including career criminals and the son of a co-conspirator, pointing to alternative killers. Following appellate intervention, unanimous rulings, and support from public figures, Tankleff was finally freed and later became a defense attorney.
stichpunkte: Marty Tankleff was convicted of murdering his parents in 1990 based on a coerced confession and a lack of emotion.
Retired detective Jay Salpeter joined the defense and found career criminal Glenn Harris, who confessed to acting as a getaway driver for two hitmen.
Additional witnesses, including a botched-hit participant and a drug enforcer, corroborated the alternative murder plot linked to a business partner.
Joey Creeden's own son came forward after watching a media report, stating his father admitted to the killings.
A judge initially denied a new trial in 2006, but a New York appellate court unanimously overturned the conviction in 2007.
Marty was released after 19 years in prison, and the Attorney General's office dropped all charges in 2008.
Tankleff later earned a law degree, secured a $10 million settlement, and now teaches wrongful conviction courses.
The partnership with Jay Salpeter ended tragically when Salpeter pleaded guilty to harassment against Tankleff in 2022.

clips.hook: A getaway driver breaks his silence 14 years later
clips.text: In a notarized statement, a career criminal admitted he drove the escape vehicle for two men headed to a residential burglary on the night of the killings.

clips.hook: A killer's own son confronts him about the murder
clips.text: The biological child of the accused hitman pressed his father for the truth after seeing a television broadcast, receiving a direct confirmation of guilt.

clips.hook: Going from a life sentence to freedom in ten days
clips.text: Nearly two decades after his parents' deaths and his subsequent imprisonment, the appellate judges unanimously reversed the verdict, allowing him to reunite with relatives.

clips.hook: Why people initially refused to believe in his innocence
clips.text: Early media broadcasts about the disputed police admission drew widespread skepticism from the public, who insisted they would never admit to a crime they did not commit.

clips.hook: From prison cell to law professor and a multi-million payout
clips.text: Following his release from incarceration, the exonerated man pursued higher education, secured a substantial municipal settlement, and joined a university faculty.

beschreibung: When Marty Tankleff was convicted for murdering his parents in 1990, some people still had their doubts about his guilt, including Jay Salpeter, a retired detective turned private investigator. Jay found a new witness who claimed he was the getaway driver for two hitmen who had been hired to murder the Tankleffs. After nearly two decades behind bars, Marty finally got another shot at freedom. In this season finale, Erin Moriarty and retired 48 Hours producer Gail Zimmerman discuss the conclusion of Marty Tankleff's wrongful conviction case and why it's one of the most memorable stories they've ever reported.
